seo.title: Best Tea Houses in Casablanca (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the finest tea houses in Casablanca, from historic Moroccan havens to elegant French patisseries. Find your perfect spot for mint tea, pastries, and cultural immersion.

hero.subtitle: Casablanca's tea scene is a vibrant blend of traditional Moroccan hospitality and sophisticated European influences, offering everything from bustling local patisseries to serene luxury lounges.

picks.name: Pâtisserie Bennis Habous
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A true institution in Casablanca, Pâtisserie Bennis Habous has been serving exquisite Moroccan pastries for generations. Located in the charming Habous quarter, this no-frills bakery offers an authentic experience where you can enjoy traditional sweets with a strong, comforting glass of Moroccan mint tea. It's less a sit-down cafe and more a grab-and-go with a few stools, but the quality is unmatched.
picks.whatToOrder: Any assortment of Moroccan Fekkas or Kaab el Ghazal (gazelle horns) with a piping hot glass of Moroccan mint tea.
picks.insiderTip: Go early in the morning for the freshest selection and to avoid the biggest crowds. Be prepared for a bustling, authentic local experience.
picks.redditQuote: "You *have* to visit Pâtisserie Bennis Habous if you're in the Habous area. It's not fancy, but their pastries are out of this world, especially with a sweet mint tea. So authentic."

picks.name: La Sqala
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Set within the ancient ramparts of the Old Medina, La Sqala offers a magical escape in its lush, open-air garden. While known for its full Moroccan meals, their traditional tea service is an experience in itself. The tranquil atmosphere, ornate architecture, and the gentle sound of fountains make it an ideal spot for a leisurely afternoon tea, accompanied by a selection of local pastries.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Sqala Tea Ceremony' which includes a pot of Moroccan mint tea and an assortment of local cookies and pastries.
picks.insiderTip: Reserve a table in advance, especially during peak lunch or dinner hours, even if you're just going for tea. The garden fills up quickly.
picks.redditQuote: "La Sqala's garden is an absolute dream for tea. Felt like stepping back in time, and their mint tea with those little biscuits was just perfect. Best ambiance in Casablanca, hands down."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Amoud
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pâtisserie Amoud is one of Casablanca's most renowned establishments, blending classic French patisserie techniques with authentic Moroccan flavors. With multiple elegant locations, the Maârif branch offers a sophisticated setting for enjoying meticulously crafted pastries, cakes, and a variety of teas, from traditional Moroccan mint to fine black teas. It's a popular spot for both locals and visitors.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Tarte au Citron Meringuée' (Lemon Meringue Tart) or a selection of mini Moroccan pastries, paired with Moroccan mint tea or a classic Earl Grey.
picks.insiderTip: They also have a fantastic selection of breads. Consider grabbing a fresh baguette to go after your tea and pastry.
picks.redditQuote: "Amoud is my go-to for a fancy tea break. Their French pastries are divine, and the atmosphere is so chic. Always a good choice for a quiet afternoon in Casablanca."

picks.name: Maârif Pastry
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A bustling local favorite, Maârif Pastry offers an extensive selection of fresh Moroccan and some French-inspired pastries at very reasonable prices. It's a lively spot, popular for a quick breakfast or an afternoon tea break. While the decor is simple, the quality of the sweets and the friendly, efficient service make it a must-visit for those seeking good value and authentic local flavors.
picks.whatToOrder: A selection of 'Briouats' (sweet almond pastries) and a glass of hot Moroccan mint tea.
picks.insiderTip: It can get quite busy, especially in the late afternoon. Be prepared to stand or share a small table.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want good, cheap, and authentic Moroccan pastries, Maârif Pastry is the spot. Their tea is strong and sweet, just how I like it. Perfect for a quick sugar fix."

picks.name: Le Casablanca Hotel Tea Lounge
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For a truly luxurious tea experience, the elegant tea lounge at Le Casablanca Hotel provides a sophisticated setting. With plush seating, refined decor, and impeccable service, it's the perfect place for a traditional afternoon tea or a quiet rendezvous. They offer a selection of premium teas, both local and international, complemented by exquisite pastries, mini sandwiches, and scones.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Afternoon Tea Set' which includes a variety of savory and sweet bites, along with your choice of tea.
picks.insiderTip: Dress smart casual to fit the upscale ambiance. Reservations are recommended for afternoon tea, especially on weekends.
picks.redditQuote: "My wife and I splurged on afternoon tea at Le Casablanca Hotel and it was fantastic. Such a beautiful setting and the pastries were tiny works of art. A real treat!"

picks.name: Paul
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The French bakery chain Paul has several popular locations in Casablanca, offering a consistent and reliable experience for those craving classic European pastries and good coffee or tea. The Anfa Place Mall branch provides lovely sea views from its terrace, making it a pleasant spot for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy fresh croissants, macarons, and a range of teas in a chic, comfortable setting.
picks.whatToOrder: A 'Pain au Chocolat' or 'Macaron' with a 'Thé à la Menthe' (mint tea) or a 'Thé Noir' (black tea).
picks.insiderTip: The outdoor seating at the Anfa Place Mall location offers refreshing sea breezes and great people-watching.
picks.redditQuote: "Can always count on Paul for a solid tea and pastry. It's not Moroccan traditional, but sometimes you just want a good croissant and their mint tea is surprisingly decent! The view from Anfa Place is a bonus."

picks.name: Rick's Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Immortalized by the movie 'Casablanca,' Rick's Cafe offers a unique blend of nostalgia and Moroccan charm. While primarily a restaurant and bar, they do serve tea and coffee in their iconic setting. It's more about the experience and ambiance than a dedicated tea house, but enjoying a Moroccan mint tea while soaking in the legendary atmosphere and listening to live piano music is truly special.
picks.whatToOrder: Moroccan Mint Tea, to fully embrace the local culture within the iconic setting.
picks.insiderTip: Visiting in the late afternoon for tea means you can enjoy the ambiance before the dinner rush and live music starts, which can make it very crowded.
picks.redditQuote: "Had to visit Rick's Cafe, obviously. It's touristy, but still cool. Just grabbed a mint tea to soak it all in. Definitely worth it for the history and atmosphere alone, even if you don't stay for dinner."

picks.name: Othmane Pastry
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Othmane Pastry is a well-regarded local patisserie known for its wide array of high-quality Moroccan sweets and savory snacks. It offers a clean, modern, and inviting space for a relaxed tea break. Their selection often includes lesser-known regional specialties alongside popular favorites, making it a great spot for adventurous palates looking to sample various Moroccan treats with their tea.
picks.whatToOrder: Try their 'Sellou' (a sweet, nutty paste) or a 'Chabakia' (honey cookie) with a traditional Moroccan mint tea.
picks.insiderTip: They often have seasonal pastries, so ask about any special offerings when you visit.
picks.redditQuote: "Othmane Pastry is a hidden gem in Gautier. Their sweets are always so fresh and they have such a good variety. I loved trying their different pastries with my mint tea."

picks.name: Dar Dada
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in the heart of the Habous quarter, Dar Dada is an authentic Moroccan restaurant that also excels in providing a lovely tea experience. Its warm, inviting decor, featuring traditional Moroccan craftsmanship, creates a cozy atmosphere perfect for unwinding. While you can enjoy full meals, their tea service with homemade pastries is a delightful way to soak in Moroccan hospitality.
picks.whatToOrder: A pot of traditional Moroccan mint tea served with a plate of their homemade Moroccan cookies.
picks.insiderTip: Combine your visit with some shopping in the surrounding Habous souks for a full cultural immersion.
picks.redditQuote: "Dar Dada in Habous has such a welcoming vibe. We stopped for tea after exploring the market and it was the perfect calm oasis. The tea and cookies were excellent."

picks.name: L'Etoile Centrale
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A historic fixture in Casablanca's city center, L'Etoile Centrale is a classic Moroccan cafe with a strong French influence. It's known for its spacious outdoor terrace, making it an excellent spot for people-watching in the bustling heart of the city. Enjoy a traditional Moroccan mint tea or a coffee with a selection of pastries in a vibrant, slightly old-world setting that captures the essence of downtown Casablanca.
picks.whatToOrder: A 'Thé à la Menthe' and a 'Mille-feuille' (Napoleon pastry) while watching the city go by.
picks.insiderTip: Grab an outdoor table for the best experience, but be prepared for a lively and sometimes noisy atmosphere, especially during rush hours.
picks.redditQuote: "L'Etoile Centrale is classic Casablanca. Not the fanciest, but perfect for a cheap tea and just watching the world go by. It's got that old-school charm."

picks.name: Pâtisserie La Comtesse
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pâtisserie La Comtesse offers a refined French patisserie experience in Casablanca. Known for its exquisite cakes, delicate pastries, and artisanal chocolates, this elegant tea house is a perfect retreat for those with a sweet tooth. The ambiance is chic and sophisticated, providing a serene backdrop for enjoying high-quality teas paired with beautiful, handcrafted desserts.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Opéra Cake' or a 'Religieuse' with a traditional Moroccan mint tea or a delicate green tea.
picks.insiderTip: They also create custom cakes for special occasions, so keep it in mind if you're celebrating anything in Casablanca.
picks.redditQuote: "La Comtesse is where I go when I want to feel fancy. Their French pastries are stunning, almost too pretty to eat, and the tea selection is top-notch. Great spot for a special treat."

picks.name: Palais Dar Souiri
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Housed within a beautifully restored traditional Moroccan palace in the Habous district, Palais Dar Souiri offers a regal setting for dining and enjoying tea. The opulent decor, intricate zellige tile work, and grand courtyards transport you to another era. While it serves full meals, their traditional tea service is a delightful way to experience the grandeur and hospitality of Moroccan culture.
picks.whatToOrder: A traditional Moroccan 'Thé à la Menthe' served in a silver teapot with a selection of regional 'Ghoriba' cookies.
picks.insiderTip: Explore the different rooms and courtyards, each offering unique architectural details and photo opportunities.
picks.redditQuote: "The setting at Palais Dar Souiri is incredible. It feels like you're in a royal palace just for tea. The mint tea itself was strong and delicious, and the whole experience was just magical."

faq.question: What is Moroccan mint tea, and why is it so popular?
faq.answer: Moroccan mint tea, or 'Atay,' is a sweet green tea prepared with fresh spearmint leaves and a generous amount of sugar. It's a cornerstone of Moroccan hospitality and culture, offered to guests as a sign of welcome and enjoyed throughout the day. Its popularity stems from its refreshing taste, its role in social rituals, and its invigorating properties, making it an essential part of Moroccan daily life.

faq.question: Are tea houses in Casablanca suitable for families with children?
faq.answer: Most tea houses in Casablanca, especially traditional ones and larger cafes, are very welcoming to families. Places like La Sqala with its garden, or Pâtisserie Amoud with more space, are particularly suitable. Smaller, bustling local bakeries might be less comfortable for very young children, but generally, Moroccan culture embraces children in public spaces, making tea time a family-friendly activity.

faq.question: What kind of pastries should I try with my tea in Casablanca?
faq.answer: You must try traditional Moroccan pastries like Kaab el Ghazal (gazelle horns, almond paste wrapped in delicate dough), Fekkas (crispy anise and almond biscuits), Ghriba (chewy almond or coconut cookies), and Chabakia (honey-drenched sesame cookies, especially popular during Ramadan). Many tea houses also offer French-inspired pastries like croissants, macarons, and tarts due to colonial influence.

faq.question: What is the typical etiquette for drinking tea in Morocco?
faq.answer: When served Moroccan mint tea, it's polite to accept at least two or three glasses as a sign of respect for your host. Tea is traditionally poured from a height to create froth and aerate the tea, so don't be surprised by this ritual. You don't need to finish every drop, but showing appreciation for the effort is customary. It's also acceptable to decline more tea after a few glasses.

faq.question: Can I find non-mint tea options in Casablanca tea houses?
faq.answer: While Moroccan mint tea is ubiquitous, many of the more modern or upscale tea houses and hotel lounges in Casablanca offer a wider selection of teas. You can often find black teas (like Earl Grey or English Breakfast), green teas, herbal infusions, and sometimes even specialty blends. Traditional local bakeries might have fewer options beyond mint tea, but cafes like Paul or Pâtisserie Amoud will certainly cater to diverse preferences.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian or vegan options available at Casablanca tea houses?
faq.answer: Many Moroccan pastries are naturally vegetarian, as they are often almond or honey-based, but may contain eggs and butter. Vegan options are less common but can be found; you might need to inquire about specific ingredients. Moroccan mint tea itself is typically vegan (green tea, mint, sugar), but always clarify if you have strict dietary requirements. Some modern cafes might offer plant-based milk alternatives for coffee, but less so for traditional tea.

methodology: Our selection of Casablanca's best tea houses is based on extensive research, including local expert recommendations, aggregated user reviews, and in-person visits. We prioritize authenticity, quality of offerings, ambiance, and overall visitor experience to ensure a diverse and top-tier list.
